Beauty Bar 6 Ea' $13.99 -> $11.192 are PER-PACK prices on a per-bar commodity, 6 bars never divided: true 1.812 and 1.865/bar), 2 wrong-product ('Reese's Mini Pumpkins Chocolate Candy & Peanut Butter Creme 7 Oz', 'Reese's Peanut Butter Skeletons 8.1 Oz' on peanut-butter), 2 undecidable from the row (Dove Cleansing Bar 5 Oz $7.99; Dove deodorant 1.7 Oz $14.99)

items.root_cause: the multibuy branch prices an each-unit commodity per PACK when the pack count is in the name ('6 Ea') rather than the size field, and then blames every band refusal on the parse, so a real premium sale and a real basis bug page identically as NEW price flags and neither reaches the right owner

root_fix.what: resolve the pack count, then say which half a refusal is
root_fix.exact_change: compare-deals multibuy each-basis: when the commodity unit is each and the name states N (ea|ct|count|pk|pack|bars) with N>1 and the size field states no count, divide the multibuy price by N (resolve by proof as the Aldi builder does: refuse, never guess, when name and size disagree). At :3035 the reason names its half: 'OUT-OF-BAND on a complete basis (the band refuses a real price; see band review)' vs 'OUT-OF-BAND with an unresolved pack count (review the capture)'. check-ad-cycles:3298 keys only the unresolved half as MULTIBUY price flags; the complete-basis half goes to audit-band-refusals' open rows. :3529 says 'not published' for MULTIBUY lines

evidence: LANE MEASUREMENT CONFIRMED for its 4 rows (0 hold a cell) and EXTENDED: a count-basis read of all 464 each-unit store cells on comparison-2026-09-23 finds 2 live wrong-basis cells no bar flags: tea-bags @ Aldi 'Benner Black Tea Bags 100 CT' size field '24 ct' -> per-24-pack 0.0621 (the name says 100: 0.0149, which would CROWN tea-bags over Walmart 0.0204); facial-tissues @ Aldi 'Willow Facial Tissue 144 CT' size field '160 ct' -> 0.0087 (144: 0.0097); both as_of 2026-08-05

the cheap side of the band backlog is this class: 13 of 1,091 keys are BELOW the floor and 10 of those are a sub-unit count read as the unit (Walmart paper-towels x6 at 0.0253-0.0304 per 'each' from sheet counts, e.g. '2 Triple Rolls, 123 Sheets per Roll' 246 ct; bread x3 per slice from '20 Count'; Baker's parchment 'Pre-Cut Sheets 35 ct')
the same class keeps Walmart off two staples: Walmart paper-towels 133 of 136 rows and toilet-paper 156 of 157 rows carry a SHEET count as their size; neither commodity has a Walmart cell

surface_fix.what: no per-cell fix: the refusal below is the fix

items.root_cause: the engine takes an each-commodity's count from the size field without checking it against a count the name states, so a card count that disagrees with its own name (Aldi) or a sub-unit count (sheets, slices) becomes the basis; below the derived floor the band hides it, inside the floor nothing reads it

root_fix.what: a COUNT-CONFLICT refusal in the one refusal chain
root_fix.exact_change: Get-FirstRefusal gains 'count-conflict' ahead of 'band': for an each-unit commodity, when the name states a pack count N (ct|count|pk|pack|ea|bags|rolls) and the basis count M comes from the size field with M != N and neither is a multiple of the other (the 'N pk., M ct.' total form stays legal), or the only count present is a sub-unit ('sheets per roll', 'N count' on a loaf), refuse with basis 'COUNT-CONFLICT' and flag it (the store falls through to its next row). No band, no threshold

open_questions_for_brad.question: 1,077 of the 1,091 band-backlog rows are real-looking products ABOVE the derived price ceiling (shampoo 54, hand-soap 36, toothbrushes 32, the Dove sales that paged on 09-23). A dear row can only show as a store's own cell when that store has nothing cheaper. Should the ceiling keep refusing them?
options: A: keep the ceiling as it is. The dear rows stay off the board, nothing pages, and the backlog is recorded as by-design (a dear wrong product, like candy on peanut-butter, also stays off).

B: drop the ceiling for rows whose basis is complete (the multibuy split in 9459a1 says which), keep the floor. Real premium prices can show as a store's cell; every dear wrong product then needs an identity exclude first, which is 1,077 decisions of matching work.
C: keep the ceiling but have it flag instead of refuse for everyday rows. Same board exposure as B, with a review list instead of an exclude backlog.
open_questions_for_brad.recommendation: A: the board shows the cheapest real price per store, a premium row almost never changes what a shopper sees, and B or C trade the ceiling's quiet protection against dear wrong products for weeks of exclude work
open_questions_for_brad.consequence_of_no_answer: nothing moves on the board; 0c812e stays open as a record

open_questions_for_brad.question: Walmart lists paper towels and toilet paper by SHEET count, so 289 Walmart rows cannot be priced per roll and Walmart has no cell for either. The other stores are priced per roll, treating a double or mega roll the same as a regular one. How should these two be compared?
options: A: per roll, as today. The engine reads the roll count from Walmart's names ('6 Triple Rolls'), Walmart gets a cell, and roll size is still ignored everywhere.

B: per 100 sheets. Every store needs a sheet count (Walmart gives it; most names say 'N Sheets per Roll'; rows without one are refused). The honest comparison, but it may drop cells at stores that never state sheets.
C: leave Walmart out of both commodities.
open_questions_for_brad.recommendation: B is the more accurate comparison and A the cheaper change; either needs a count of which stores' rows state sheets before it ships
open_questions_for_brad.consequence_of_no_answer: Walmart stays off two staples; its rows are refused as COUNT-CONFLICT (8d2ad5) rather than OUT-OF-BAND

Also pepperoncini priced by banana pepper rings (3).
options: A: accept both: a summer squash prices zucchini and any pasta shape prices pasta by the pound, recorded as reviewed same-food so the audit stops counting them.
B: split them: zucchini and yellow squash become two commodities, and each pasta shape its own commodity where Omaha stores carry it; recipes whose shape has no cell are held until one does.
C: split zucchini only, keep pasta shapes as one food.
